key_insight: The NTIRE 2026 Efficient SR challenge shows that carefully designed lightweight networks can substantially cut runtime, parameter count, and FLOPs while keeping PSNR near 26.9 dB on DIV2K_LSDIR benchmarks.
problem_solved: Designing single-image super-resolution models that balance high reconstruction quality with strict efficiency constraints (runtime, parameters, FLOPs) for practical deployment.
method: Organized a public challenge (95 registered, 15 valid submissions) to benchmark efficiency-focused SR designs on DIV2K_LSDIR_valid and DIV2K_LSDIR_test with target PSNR ≈ 26.90–26.99 dB.
Teams applied lightweight architectural choices (e.g., pruning, efficient blocks, mobile-friendly convolutions) and optimization/training tweaks to trade computation for minimal PSNR loss.
Systematic analysis and leaderboard comparisons highlighted practical trade-offs between PSNR, runtime, parameter count, and FLOPs.
impact: Provides a practical roadmap and empirical baselines for ML practitioners aiming to deploy SR on resource-constrained devices, and clarifies where efficiency gains are possible without sacrificing measurable quality.
